alt.en: A black-and-white photograph of a rocky hillside with olive trees and long stone field walls. A person in a head covering sits on the rocks in the foreground, and the houses of a town line the ridge in the distance under a pale sky.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de una ladera rocosa con olivos y largos muros de piedra entre los campos. En primer plano, una persona con la cabeza cubierta está sentada sobre las rocas, y a lo lejos las casas de una ciudad se extienden por la cresta bajo un cielo claro.

caption.en: Safed, "a city built on a hill" as the negative's caption calls it, above stone-walled fields, photographed by the American Colony of Jerusalem between 1898 and 1914; in Alkabetz's century the mystics of this town walked out into the fields on Friday afternoons to meet the Sabbath.
caption.es: Safed, "una ciudad asentada sobre un monte", como la llama el rótulo del negativo, sobre campos con muros de piedra, fotografiada por la American Colony de Jerusalén entre 1898 y 1914; en el siglo de Alkabetz, los místicos de esta ciudad salían a los campos los viernes por la tarde para recibir al sabbat.

source: Northern views. Safed "A city built on a hill" / American Colony, Jerusalem (glass dry plate negative, 10 x 12 in.)
library: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, G. Eric and Edith Matson Photograph Collection
licenceEvidence: LoC item record, Rights Advisory: "No known restrictions on publication." (https://www.loc.gov/pictures/item/mpc2004007387/PP/, read via the Wayback Machine copy of 2017-06-08). Photograph made 1898 to 1914 by the American Colony Photo Dept., no individual named (see rights.md).
credit: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, Matson Photograph Collection, LC-DIG-matpc-07029

alt.en: A printed page of Hebrew prayer-book text with vowel points, headed "Kabbalat Shabbat" in Hebrew and numbered 112, set as five short paragraphs, each ending with the small word "Lecha", the cue for the refrain.
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro de oraciones en hebreo con vocales, con el encabezado "Kabbalat Shabbat" en hebreo y el número 112, en cinco párrafos breves que terminan cada uno con la pequeña palabra "Lecha", la señal del estribillo.

caption.en: Lecha Dodi, from the second half of verse 2 to verse 6, in Simeon Singer's Authorised Daily Prayer Book (London, 1904), the prayer book that Israel Abrahams' Companion, one of this page's sources, was written to accompany.
caption.es: Lecha Dodi, desde la segunda mitad de la estrofa 2 hasta la estrofa 6, en el Authorised Daily Prayer Book de Simeon Singer (Londres, 1904), el libro de oraciones al que acompaña el Companion de Israel Abrahams, una de las fuentes de esta página.

source: The Authorised Daily Prayer Book of the United Hebrew Congregations of the British Empire, with a new translation by S. Singer, seventh edition (London: Eyre and Spottiswoode, 5664/1904), p. 112 (Hebrew); cropped after verse 6
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published London 1904 (title page: "Seventh edition ... Eyre and Spottiswoode ... 5664 - 1904"); translator and editor Simeon Singer died 1906, Nathan Marcus Adler 1890; the Hebrew poem is Alkabetz's, 16th century. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Robarts Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: Printed music headed "LEKAH DODI (Melody for 'Omer Weeks)": a single melody line in 3/4 time over four staves, marked "p Andantino", with the English words "How lovely is the Day of Rest" under the notes and a refrain beginning "Then come, my friend, to meet the Bride".
alt.es: Música impresa con el título "LEKAH DODI (Melody for 'Omer Weeks)": una sola línea melódica en 3/4 en cuatro pentagramas, marcada "p Andantino", con la letra inglesa "How lovely is the Day of Rest" bajo las notas y un estribillo que empieza "Then come, my friend, to meet the Bride".

caption.en: Francis L. Cohen's printing of the old melody for the Omer weeks, with English words, in The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 7 (New York, 1904), p. 677: the same tune with its rhythms evened, which our arrangement is checked against.
caption.es: La impresión de Francis L. Cohen de la antigua melodía de las semanas del Ómer, con letra en inglés, en la Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 7 (Nueva York, 1904), p. 677: la misma melodía con el ritmo igualado, con la que se coteja nuestro arreglo.

source: Cyrus Adler and Francis L. Cohen, "Lekah Dodi", The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 7 (New York and London: Funk and Wagnalls, 1904), p. 677, "Lekah Dodi (Melody for 'Omer Weeks)"
library: University of California Libraries (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York 1904 ("Copyright, 1904, by Funk & Wagnalls Company"); article by Cyrus Adler (died 1940) and Francis L. Cohen (died 1934). Internet Archive marks the copy NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive
